explanation.text: The Logic: An option premium has two conceptual components: intrinsic value (the amount by which the option is in-the-money — the payoff if exercised immediately) and time value (the additional amount the market is willing to pay for the chance that the option moves further in-the-money before expiry). Both pieces add together to make the premium, so 'intrinsic value + time value' is the standard decomposition. The Trap: 'Only intrinsic value' ignores time value, the dominant component for at-the-money and out-of-the-money options. 'Only time value' is wrong for in-the-money options, which clearly have intrinsic value. 'Only interest' is unrelated — interest enters indirectly through pricing models but is not a premium component. Note: The decomposition of option premium into intrinsic value plus time value is not given in the cited NISM Series XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook pages checked, which state only that an option is bought for a premium. The framing above is presented as general options-pricing knowledge rather than as a workbook citation.
